data.title: Log Sanitizer
data.solution:
import sys
import re

def sanitize(s):
    # 1. Anti-overlapping rule
    # If 'token=' appears consecutively, we do not mask the API token
    if "token=token=" not in s:
        # API Token Rule
        # (^|[^a-zA-Z0-9]) -> Left boundary (start of line or non-alphanumeric character)
        # token=           -> The exact pattern
        # ([a-zA-Z0-9]+)   -> The value (at least 1 alphanumeric character)
        # (?=[^a-zA-Z0-9]|$) -> Right boundary (lookahead to not consume the character)
        s = re.sub(
            r"(^|[^a-zA-Z0-9])token=([a-zA-Z0-9]+)(?=[^a-zA-Z0-9]|$)",
            r"\1token=[TOKEN_REDACTED]",
            s
        )

    # 2. Credit Card Rule
    # The execution order naturally handles priority: 
    # if token=1234-5678..., the '1234' is already masked by the API step above,
    # thus invalidating the rest of the string for credit card detection.
    
    # (?<![a-zA-Z0-9-]) -> Lookbehind: no letter, digit, or hyphen before
    # (?:\d{4}-){3}\d{4} -> Exactly 4 blocks of 4 digits
    # (?![a-zA-Z0-9-])  -> Lookahead: no letter, digit, or hyphen after
    card_regex = r"(?<![a-zA-Z0-9-])(?:\d{4}-){3}\d{4}(?![a-zA-Z0-9-])"
    s = re.sub(card_regex, "[CARD_REDACTED]", s)

    return s

n = int(input())
for _ in range(n):
    line = input()
    print(sanitize(line))
data.statement:
<<Tokens>> are bounded by non-alphanumeric characters or the beginning or end of the line.

Inspect a stream of server log lines and sanitize all occurrences of the following two patterns, subject to the overlapping rule:

1. <<Credit card numbers:>> Exactly four consecutive tokens, each consisting of exactly 4 decimal digits and joined by {{-}}, form a credit card number and should be replaced with {{[CARD_REDACTED]}}.

2. <<API token:>> A token {{token}}, immediately followed by {{=}} and another token (the <<value>>) consisting of one or more alphanumeric characters, forms an API token. Redact the value token only, replacing it with {{[TOKEN_REDACTED]}}.

<<Overlapping rule:>>
Overlapping occurrences of a single pattern should not be considered to fit the pattern and must remain unchanged. For example:
• Five or more consecutive 4-digit tokens joined by {{-}}.
• {{token=}} appearing consecutively two or more times.

If {{token=}} is immediately followed by a credit card number, sanitize the API token value first.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

Tokens are bounded by non-alphanumeric characters or the beginning or end of the line.

Inspect a stream of server log lines and sanitize all occurrences of the following two patterns, subject to the overlapping rule:

1. Credit card numbers: Exactly four consecutive tokens, each consisting of exactly 4 decimal digits and joined by -, form a credit card number and should be replaced with [CARD_REDACTED].

2. API token: A token token, immediately followed by = and another token (the value) consisting of one or more alphanumeric characters, forms an API token. Redact the value token only, replacing it with [TOKEN_REDACTED].

Overlapping rule:
Overlapping occurrences of a single pattern should not be considered to fit the pattern and must remain unchanged. For example:
• Five or more consecutive 4-digit tokens joined by -.
• token= appearing consecutively two or more times.

If token= is immediately followed by a credit card number, sanitize the API token value first.
Input
Line 1: An integer N for the number of log lines.
Next N lines: A string line representing a raw log entry.
Output
N lines: The sanitized log entries.
Constraints
1 ≤ N ≤ 10
line contains between 1 and 100 printable ASCII characters.
Example
Input
2
Payment: card 1234-5678-9012-3456 verified.
GET /auth?token=abC123XyZ
Output
Payment: card [CARD_REDACTED] verified.
GET /auth?token=[TOKEN_REDACTED]
